chunks: Ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from Ḥammād, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked him about a man who died and left children, while some of them were absent and it was not known where he was. He said: "His inheritance is to be divided, and the absent one's share is to be set aside."
I said: "Is zakat due on it?" He said: "No, not until he returns, takes possession of it, and a year passes over it."
I said: "What if it is not known where he is?" He said: "If the heirs are financially well-off, they may divide his inheritance; then if he comes, they must return it to him."

key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: the obligatory alms-tax due on qualifying wealth
key_terms.يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ: that one full lunar year passes over it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the inheritance and zakat of a missing heir whose whereabouts are unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the inheritance of an absent heir whose whereabouts are unknown. His share is initially set aside, and zakat is not due on it until he returns, takes possession, and a full year passes. If the heirs are financially capable, they may divide the estate, but they must restore the absent person's share if he returns.
